mechanism_narrative: The INSR-OSMR forced-proximity novokine (flexible_GS4, ~20 Å) brings an RTK (INSR, Tyr kinase domain at 1023-1298) into direct co-clustering with a type I cytokine receptor (OSMR, JAK1-associated). INSR's kinase transphosphorylates OSMR's JAK1-docking sites, while OSMR-associated JAK1/2 transphosphorylates INSR's juxtamembrane IRS1/2 docking motifs — creating a hybrid insulin-cytokine signalosome. The biased output is dominated by GRB2-SHC1-RAS-MAPK and IRS1/2-PI3K-AKT pathways (via transphosphorylation-recruited adaptors), plus JAK-STAT5 signaling from OSMR's JAK1 platform. PLCG1/2 and RASA1 are sterically excluded because the short GS4 linker (~20 Å) positions the INSR kinase domain too close to the OSMR intracellular face for PLCγ's large PH-SH2-SH3 module to bridge productively. VAV1 is excluded due to the absence of ITAM motifs in this receptor pair. The resulting transcriptome signature upregulates muscle structural/contractile genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN) and ECM remodeling factors (IGFBP7, TIMP3, ITGA8) while suppressing aged-marker IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN), inflammatory mediators (IL32, TXNIP), and the myogenic differentiation factor MYF5 — consistent with a rejuvenating shift toward the young muscle phenotype.
